newsitem.title: MEXICO: Trial Mexican crude seen hitting U.S. West Coast.
newsitem.headline: Trial Mexican crude seen hitting U.S. West Coast.

text.p: West Coast refineries are eyeing possible test shipments of Mexican heavy Maya crude as soon as next month, traders said.
An independent West Coast refinery trader told Reuters the company is keen on a trial run of the crude in the near future.
It would be the first time since 1991 that state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) has sold crude to West Coast refineries.
"There is definite interest in putting (Maya) on the West Coast in July," another trader at a southern California refinery that runs heavy crudes said.
Mexican heavy Maya crude is high in sulphur (API 22), which traders say has complicated the sale to West Coast refineries because of strict emission standards in Southern California.
But traders say fewer restrictions are in place in northern California and Washington state.
West Coast refiners are generally been tight-lipped about any plans, but Pemex traders have said they are in negotiations to sell contracts to the region and expect to close deals "soon".
The price formula for West Coast shipments of Maya would be an average of West Texas Intermediate (WTI), Alaska North Slope (ANS), and Kern River grades minus a constant discount, traders said.
"You could probably look at the Gulf Coast's formula and assume...its going to be a lower price," the southern California refinery trader said.
Pemex will initially sell a few spot contracts of Maya then follow up with term contracts once refiners are comfortable processing the grade, traders said.
By moving barrels to the West Coast, Pemex aims to tighten supplies and keep prices higher in their prime market, the U.S. Gulf.
In the face of greater production in 1997 and projected output for the coming years, Pemex traders say they are looking to sell "wherever they can."
In May, Pemex sent its first-ever shipment to South Africa, as part of a request by Texaco Inc.. The one-time sale was of about 30,700 barrels per day for the month, Pemex said.
Pemex has also moved to lessen its reliance on U.S. clients and boost its European clientele.
